model.files.mediaFiles

Class MyFilesHolder

  • java.lang.Object
    • model.files.common.BaseFile<T>
      • model.files.common.JsonFile<MyFileModel>
        • model.files.mediaFiles.MyFilesHolder
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    IFileMethods<MyFileModel>

    public final class MyFilesHolder
extends JsonFile<MyFileModel>
    This is my files holder singleton implementation for holding the single ref point to files.json, and it's also used to parse and return the file objects from the file.

    RazvanNuta

      • ParseFile

        public HashMap<Integer,MyFileModel> ParseFile(HashMap<Integer,LocationModel> locationsMap)
                                       throws DataFileException
        This method is used to parse the media files from files.json, after the locations were parsed from locations.json. The locations are needed to check that each media file belongs to a monitored location and that its path is the path of that location followed by its name.
        Parameters:
        locationsMap - The locations parsed from locations.json, by id
        Returns:
        The valid media files from files.json, by id
        Throws:
        DataFileException - In the case files.json cannot be read or it does not contain a valid JSON throws this exception.
        See Also:
        JsonFile.ParseFile(), MyLocationsHolder

      • parseJSON

        protected List<MyFileModel> parseJSON(String jsonStr)
        This method is used to parse the media files from the content of files.json and to validate each one of them. A media file with a missing or invalid field is ignored and a message is printed, for example when its id is duplicated, its location is not monitored, its extension is not supported or does not match its name and type, its size is negative, its date is not in the dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm format or its path is not the path of its location followed by its name.
        Specified by:
        parseJSON in class JsonFile<MyFileModel>
        Parameters:
        jsonStr - The content of files.json
        Returns:
        The valid media files from files.json
        See Also:
        MediaType
